mergeOrderAndPinChoice.noRedOrSkippedWindow: While #474 is held, engine main carries no declaration file. Reading only main would make engine-declaration-pin red on every push until #474 merged -- a dead gate -- and buying green by skipping when the file is missing is refused in advance ('a missing engine file is a failure with its own message, never a pass'). The third option is what is built: the job reads main, and ONLY when main carries no declaration reads the engine's lane ref as a DECLARED fallback, printing which ref it read; every leg is still compared and absence at both refs still refuses. Nothing is skipped and no CI is red by design in either window.
mergeOrderAndPinChoice.theOppositeOrderRecorded: Engine-first was the lane's FIRST design and is recorded rather than dropped. It also leaves no CI red (the engine's declaration is checked offline against its own pin facts and never reads the factory at runtime; the fallback covers the window), so it was not a red-window fix. It was still the wrong order: it opens a stretch in which the ENGINE's committed declaration asserts that the factory declares 0.05 while the factory's main still declares 0.5 -- the program's one number inconsistent, in the repo that had not moved yet, with only a lane branch bridging it. Factory-first is the order in which the two declarations agree at every moment after the first merge, and it is the order now stated in both PR bodies, in the CI job's comment, and in the check's own ENGINE_DECLARATION_UNREADABLE refusal (commit c6e14e3 corrected that prose; the lane's earlier draft said the opposite).

leave_behind: The two registers are still not joined: the factory's DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS (wired/unwired) and the engine's DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS are separate artifacts, and a destructive writer added to NEITHER repo's scan is the named bypass. Joining them (one artifact, both repos' writers, a test that the union is scanned) is a row no one owns yet.

The factory's engine-declaration-pin job runs on push/PR only. If the engine repo changes without a factory push, this job does not run until the next factory push; the engine's own CI catches a lone engine edit through the pin's internal-facts leg, but a SCHEDULED arm of the same job would close the window outright.

building-footprint-absence-supersede-delete is correctly unwired and its reason HOLDS at 0.05, but it wants a COUNT bound (n rows touched / n rows in the layer), not a share: its normal outcome is a share near 1.0, so a share guard there is a permanently-red gate. The count bound is the thing to build.

The engine's site-plan manifest byte-identity control is nondeterministic (605423 vs 605439 bytes on identical input) and can redden any engine PR's CI, including #474's after it merges to main. It is a control whose job is byte-determinism; it needs an owner.

26 factory tests fail in this Windows environment at HEAD and 27 at the same base commit 0f4558a4 -- pre-existing, none of them a guard/P-327/P-361 test, but a Windows seat re-running the suite will meet them; the vocabulary/setback/envelope/LDT-drift files listed in CP2 are the set.

Direction two of the cross-repo check (engine reads factory) is structurally un-CI-able while hauska-factory is private and unpublished; it stays a seat/local re-derivation with --factory <clone>. If a published factory artifact ever exists (or a mirror), that direction becomes enforceable and should be wired.

Prediction to check after deploy: all six counties' gate-scheduler and publish verdicts must be `pass` at 0.05 (P-327's census: zero new retirements). Williamson must show its 282,570 re-retirements PRINTED and the share at 0.0 -- a share near 0.4694 there would mean the re-retirement split is not being applied.

scratch.LESSON: A refused operator reads the refusal: if a check's message names the process order, that prose is as load-bearing as its comparison. This lane's check was written under engine-first and corrected to factory-first; the selftest was 8/8 both ways, so no test could have caught the stale sentence -- prose in a refusal needs the same review as the verdict it accompanies.

Pin content, not commits, when the repo squash-merges: a squash replaces the sha and leaves the blob, so a commit-addressed pin dies on the very merge it was meant to survive. Record blob sha + bytes + normalised sha256 and keep ref as provenance.
scratch.DEAD-END: Reading 'what the engine's main carries' before the engine PR merges cannot be made green by reading main alone, and it cannot be made green by skipping when the file is missing (that is the pre-refused option, 'a missing engine file is a failure with its own message, never a pass'). A DECLARED fallback ref, printed in the output, with every leg still compared, is the third option and the one that holds.

The engine's CI cannot read the private factory (GitHub API/raw 404, npm E404 on private:true): do not spend time trying to wire direction two; build the factory-side job instead (P-328's leave_behind said so, and it is right).
